Since we opened our doors in 2009, the world of commerce has evolved immensely, and so has Square. After enabling anyone to take payments and never miss a sale, we saw sellers stymied by disparate, outmoded products and tools that wouldn’t work together.

So we expanded into software and started building integrated, omnichannel solutions – to help sellers sell online, manage inventory, offer buy now, pay later functionality, book appointments, engage loyal buyers, and hire and pay staff. Across it all, we’ve embedded financial services tools at the point of sale, so merchants can access a business loan and manage their cash flow in one place. Afterpay furthers our goal to provide omnichannel tools that unlock meaningful value and growth, enabling sellers to capture the next generation shopper, increase order sizes, and compete at a larger scale.

Today, we are a partner to sellers of all sizes – large, enterprise-scale businesses with complex operations, sellers just starting, as well as merchants who began selling with Square and have grown larger over time. As our sellers grow, so do our solutions. There is a massive opportunity in front of us. We’re building a significant, meaningful, and lasting business, and we are helping sellers worldwide do the same.

The Role

Ordering directly from a restaurant or retail shop should be intuitive and feel dependable. Customers should know where their order is, hear about and easily follow updates, and get help quickly when something goes wrong.

We’re hiring a Product Manager to own that experience at Square, across food ordering and retail ecommerce. You’ll build customer experiences and seller tools for pickup, delivery, and shipping, helping businesses earn trust and bring customers back.

The problems are concrete: How do you follow an order’s progress? What should happen when a delivery runs late or an item goes missing? How do you make a refund clear, or give a seller an easy way to make things right? You’ll own the experience from the moment an order is placed through its arrival and any help needed afterward.

We’re looking for someone with a strong product sense who notices where people get confused, knows when to simplify, and cares about the details that build confidence. You’ll spend time with customers and sellers, work closely with design and engineering, and turn those insights into products that customers trust and repeatedly come back to for their next purchase.

You Will

  • Own the strategy and priorities. Set the direction for Square’s post-checkout customer experience across food ordering and retail. Use customer needs and business goals to decide which problems matter most, where to invest, and what can wait.
  • Bring the work together. At Block, engineers and people across teams also lead individual product improvements. You will connect those efforts across Square and external partners, spot gaps, resolve competing priorities, and make sure the pieces form a clear, consistent customer experience as more people prototype and ship.
  • Design and define user experiences. Work closely with design and engineering to shape key customer journeys, from tracking an order to getting help when something goes wrong. Bring personal taste and attention to detail to the flows, interactions, and communications that build trust.
  • Help the team scale through automation. Use AI and other tools to connect and automate repeatable work across customer research, analysis, prototyping, product development, and launch. Build reusable workflows, share what works, and give teams the context and tools to make good decisions independently.
  • Set the quality bar and guide important decisions. Define what good looks like and evaluate product ideas and AI-generated work against real customer scenarios. Test assumptions, give specific feedback, and keep refining until the experience is useful, clear, and dependable. Decide where AI and automation improve the experience and where human judgment matters.
  • Prototype and ship improvements yourself. Use AI tools to turn ideas into working prototypes, test them with customers, and learn quickly. Use GitHub and other developer tools to contribute changes through pull requests and work with engineers to ship improvements to production.
  • Own the outcomes. Follow work through launch and use customer feedback and data to guide improvements. Measure whether customers feel informed, get problems resolved quickly, and choose to order again, using signals like order-status inquiries, resolution time, satisfaction, and repeat purchases.

You Have

  • 6+ years of product management experience.
  • Consumer product judgment. You’ve shipped customer-facing products at scale that make complicated things feel simple. You can explain your decisions and what you learned from customer behavior.
  • Hands-on building with AI. You use AI to build working prototypes, automate recurring work, and test ideas. You can use GitHub and other tools to make a change and submit a PR. You can show what you’ve built and what you learned.
  • Taste and craft. You work closely with design and bring personal taste and a high bar for quality. You recognize generic or weak output, give specific feedback, and iterate until the experience feels thoughtful and useful.
  • Strategy and prioritization. You’ve set product direction and turned it into clear priorities. You make thoughtful tradeoffs and can explain what deserves investment and what can wait.
  • Customer research and analytical judgment. You use customer conversations, research, and behavioral data to guide decisions. You’re comfortable moving forward when the problem is ambiguous or the data is incomplete.
  • Leadership across teams. You bring people together around a clear direction, resolve disagreements, and get work shipped. You give others the context to make good decisions and keep moving.
  • Relevant experience. Experience with consumer products, ecommerce, marketplaces, or customer support is a plus, but not required. You’re curious about how businesses operate and what makes customers trust them.

DRW is a diversified trading firm with over 3 decades of experience bringing sophisticated technology and exceptional people together to operate in markets around the world. We value autonomy and the ability to quickly pivot to capture opportunities, so we operate using our own capital and trading at our own risk.

Headquartered in Chicago with offices throughout the U.S., Canada, Europe, and Asia, we trade a variety of asset classes including Fixed Income, ETFs, Equities, FX, Commodities and Energy across all major global markets. We have also leveraged our expertise and technology to expand into three non-traditional strategies: real estate, venture capital and cryptoassets.

We operate with respect, curiosity and open minds. The people who thrive here share our belief that it’s not just what we do that matters–it's how we do it. DRW is a place of high expectations, integrity, innovation and a willingness to challenge consensus.

Trader — Equities & Derivatives

We’re looking for an early-career trader with fewer than five years’ experience who is currently working at a bank, market maker or buy-side firm.

We’re open to a broad range of trading backgrounds. We believe a strong trader can learn new products and strategies, so we place more weight on judgement, analytical ability and curiosity than on experience in a particular market.

The role

You’ll help identify, evaluate and execute trading opportunities, manage risk and develop ideas across equities and derivatives. The precise remit will reflect your strengths and evolve as you build experience.

Your responsibilities will include:

  • Analysing market moves, positioning and catalysts to generate trading ideas.
  • Executing trades and managing positions within agreed risk limits.
  • Monitoring exposures, performance and changing market conditions.
  • Developing tools and research to improve trading decisions.
  • Working closely with the team to learn new products and strategies.

Your background

You should currently be in a trading role, with fewer than five years’ professional experience. Relevant backgrounds include one or more of:

  • Single-stock volatility.
  • Delta One or dividend trading.
  • Index volatility.
  • Exotic derivatives.
  • Dispersion strategies.
  • Event-driven or special situations strategies.
  • Index rebalancing.

We welcome candidates from banks, market makers and buy-side firms, including those working within specialist trading pods.

What we’re looking for

  • Strong numerical and analytical skills.
  • Sound risk judgement and a disciplined approach to trading.
  • Curiosity about markets and a willingness to learn beyond your current specialism.
  • The ability to make clear decisions under pressure.
  • Ownership of your work and an ability to collaborate effectively.
  • Coding or data-analysis skills would be useful.

You don’t need experience across every area listed. We’re looking for someone with strong foundations and the potential to develop into a versatile trader.

Founded in 2017 and headquartered in New York City, CertiK provides end-to-end security solutions including smart contract audits, penetration testing, on-chain monitoring, incident response, and compliance services for some of the largest projects in the digital asset ecosystem.

Ready to do the most impactful work of your career? At Coinbase, we are uncompromising on our mission to increase economic freedom. The bar is high, the environment is intense, and we like it that way. This isn't a place for complacency, it’s a place to be pushed past your perceived limits. If you're ready to build the future of finance alongside people who refuse to settle for "good enough," you belong here. Coinbase is a remote-first, but not remote-only company. Expect to get together quarterly for intense in-person working sessions called “surges.” learn more about working at Coinbase.

We're hiring a Senior Staff Software Engineer, Native Mobile to join the App Infra team within the Consumer & Business group as a technical architect for Coinbase's native mobile future. This is the most significant client platform shift in the company's history, replacing the React Native app with native Swift and Kotlin builds for millions of customers. Coinbase mobile engineers will be expected to support both iOS and Android on their teams using AI-driven agentic translation at unprecedented scale. You'll own outcomes spanning the App Infra team and our ~30 product teams, set our architectural patterns, and relentlessly drive Coinbase towards a novel, world-class mobile development experience.

What you'll do

  • Define the technical strategy to make the native app development future at Coinbase a reality.
  • Lead the AI-assisted migration approach, designing reusable AI-automation paradigms such as agent swarms, automated dual-repo synchronization, and continuous improvement of translation efficiency using automated feedback loops.
  • Architect a paved-road native framework in Swift and Kotlin that sets the architectural bar across teams, unlocking the ability for a single mobile contributor to be productive in both iOS and Android codebases simultaneously.
  • Drive organizational readiness as a trusted cross-functional partner with product, design, and engineering leadership, resolving cross-team blockers, de-escalating conflict during the dual-app straddle period, and holding peer leaders to a high bar so their patterns spread across teams.
  • Mentor L5-L6 engineers, develop the technical leadership pipeline for native mobile, and recruit actively through reputation, ensuring the team excels in your absence and your successor is developing.
  • Become a leader throughout the entire mobile community at Coinbase, defining best practices and fostering connection and support between all mobile engineers.

Required Skills and Experience:

  • 12+ years of software engineering experience with deep expertise in iOS or Android native mobile development (Swift/iOS or Kotlin/Android) and strong working proficiency in the other platform, operating at depth across your own and adjacent team codebases.
  • Track record of owning outcomes spanning 2-3+ teams that drive business impact, including multi-phase platform migrations or rewrites at scale where you shaped strategy and made trade-offs that raised ROI across teams.
  • Deep mobile performance expertise across iOS and Android, including cold start optimization, frame stability, scroll jank elimination, and device-tier profiling, with experience setting the architectural bar and defining ownership boundaries other teams build against.
  • Proven influence without authority at senior levels, with experience changing the technical direction of teams outside your own, securing leadership alignment on ambiguous high-stakes decisions, and resolving cross-team blockers using all tools at your disposal.
  • Experience designing AI-native engineering workflows adopted across teams, including LLM-driven code generation, agent-based automation, or reusable automation patterns that re-implement existing workflows.
  • Uses generative AI responsibly, maintaining human oversight to deliver business-ready outputs and measurable gains in workflow efficiency, cost, and quality.

Company Description

About us

Solflare is one of the fastest-growing crypto wallets in the world. With around 4 million monthly active users and over $20 billion in digital assets secured through our platform, we’re building a powerful gateway to Web3. Founded in 2021, Solflare now has a team of nearly 150 people, with offices in Zagreb, Belgrade, and Novi Sad, plus remote teams across the globe. Our vision is simple but bold: a world where everyone uses a Web3 wallet and has full control over their assets – achieving true financial independence.

Our culture

At Solflare, we’re on a mission to empower people to truly own and thrive – starting with our own team. We take on bold challenges with curiosity, grit, and a deep sense of accountability. Here, progress means learning fast, solving smart, and showing up for each other without ego. You’ll join a team where we question the status quo, celebrate shared wins, and never settle for “just good enough.” If you’re excited by growth – yours, ours, and society’s – you’ll feel right at home.

Job Description

The role

As a Senior Data Analyst at Solflare, you’ll dive deep into data to uncover insights and trends that help us make better decisions about our product and its growth. You’ll work closely with product managers, engineers, and other teams to turn complex, raw data into clear and actionable insights. Your work will directly influence important decisions, from improving existing product features and identifying opportunities for new ones to shaping our market expansion strategy.

What makes analytics at Solflare particularly interesting is the depth and variety of data available to us. Since blockchain data is public, we can analyze user behavior at the individual transaction level across the wider Solana ecosystem, not just within Solflare. This means that a user’s journey does not necessarily start when they first open or create a Solflare wallet. Blockchain data allows us to understand parts of their activity before they become a Solflare user, including which wallets and protocols they used, how they transacted, where their assets moved, and how their behavior changed after adopting Solflare.

Analyzing the blockchain gives us the opportunity to answer questions that traditional product analytics often cannot. We can track market shares, explore how users interact with competing companies, where assets are moving, and which products or behaviors are gaining traction across the ecosystem.

By combining this on-chain information with our off-chain product data, such as app activity, event tracking, and internal user data, we get a uniquely rich view of the full user journey. You might investigate what users do on-chain after using Solflare, identify behavioral patterns connected to retention or churn, or uncover opportunities for new products, features, and integrations.

If you’re excited by complex data, curious about user behavior, and ready to work in a role where your insights can directly shape product strategy and company growth, we’d love to hear from you.

Core responsibilities:

  • Data collection: You’ll gather data from a variety of sources (databases, APIs, spreadsheets) and ensure it’s accurate, complete, and relevant to the business questions at hand.
  • Data preparation: Actively contributing to our data pipeline, building and maintaining the transformation logic that turns raw data into analysis-ready datasets.
  • Exploratory analysis: Use statistical techniques and data visualization to uncover trends, patterns, and correlations in the data. This will help guide the team in making data-driven decisions.
  • Reporting & visualization: You’ll create clear and insightful dashboards, reports, and charts, making it easy for stakeholders to understand the findings and take action.
  • Collaboration with teams: Work alongside product managers, engineers, and other stakeholders to define key metrics and provide data-driven recommendations that shape the product roadmap.
  • Data integrity: Ensure that the data is secure, well-documented, and accessible to those who need it most.

Qualifications

Requirements

  • Experience: 5+ years of experience in data analysis or engineering involving large amounts of different types of data
  • Statistical analysis: Experience with hypothesis testing, A/B testing, and other statistical methods.
  • Programming & data manipulation: Proficiency in at least one programming language for data cleaning, transformation, and analysis.
  • SQL: Strong skills in writing and optimizing SQL queries to extract and aggregate data from databases.
  • Data visualization tools: Experience with business intelligence tools such as Tableau, Power BI, Looker, or similar.
  • AI-assisted development: Experience integrating AI tools (e.g. Claude Code) into your engineering workflow for faster iteration and higher-quality output
  • Spreadsheets: Solid experience using Excel or Google Sheets for quick analysis and pivot tables.
  • ETL & data workflow: Basic understanding of ETL processes and tools to move data from different sources into a usable format.

Nice to have:

  • Fintech/banking/insurance industry experience
  • Experience with processing blockchain data (e.g. using data from Dune, Solscan, etc.).

Additional Information

Personality Traits We Value

  • Problem-solvers: You see roadblocks as opportunities and don’t wait around for someone else to fix things.
  • Self-starters: You take initiative, follow through, and deliver with pride – no excuses, no shortcuts.
  • Team players: You thrive in a “we, not me” culture, lifting others up while sharing the load.
  • Adaptable minds: You embrace change, question how things are done, and constantly look for better ways.
  • Ownership mindset: You own your work end-to-end, communicate openly, and learn from every challenge.

Why Solflare?

  • Make an impact: Your work will directly shape how people interact with and understand crypto wallets, empowering users around the globe.
  • Work with the best: Collaborate with a talented, driven team across design, engineering, and product to build innovative, user-first experiences.
  • Flexibility: Remote or office – up to you. Enjoy a flexible work environment based on trust that supports your well-being and fosters creativity, as well as flexible work time – work when you are most productive, with no micromanagement.
  • Perks & benefits: individual education budget, cool team buildings, private health insurance, to name a few.
  • Learn about Crypto: No crypto experience? No problem! You’ll be part of a team that will teach you the ropes and help you grow into an expert.

Join us at Solflare and be part of something bigger than yourself. We’re not just reacting to trends; we’re building the future. If you’re ready to push boundaries, challenge assumptions, and make an impact, we want to hear from you.

Apply now and help us shape the future of decentralized finance.

About Stripe

Stripe is a technology company focused on improving the conditions for economic growth and prosperity. We build programmable financial infrastructure, rethinking from first principles how financial services should work, to make it easier and cheaper for any business to start and scale. More than 10 million businesses build on Stripe, spanning the economic frontier—from solo founders to established enterprises—united by a practical focus on growth. The most ambitious companies in the world use Stripe as core infrastructure to grow faster. They process trillions of dollars a year on Stripe, equivalent to around 1.6% of global GDP. We build entirely new pieces of financial infrastructure to enable new ideas. And our significant advances in risk and fraud infrastructure over many years are making the internet economy safer and more accessible.  

Though people at Stripe don’t tend to take themselves seriously, Stripe is a fairly serious place: our customers are depending on us for their livelihoods. We admire ambition, intensity, curiosity, humility, and rigor. The most effective people become knowledgeable about many domains besides their own. Any company is an applied exercise in understanding some aspect of society or the market. In working with so many (especially the new and innovative ones), we think that Stripe is one of the very best places to learn about how the world works.

What you’ll do

As an intern at Stripe you’ll work on projects across our stack that directly impact the way millions of businesses operate. You’ll own problems end to end with the support of your manager and teammates. It’s an opportunity to work alongside some of the most creative and technically rigorous engineers in the industry and learn how to ship high-quality work at scale. By contributing to Stripe’s codebase you’ll work across domains that give you insight into how the global economy works. Recent intern projects include expanding Stripe’s Payments Foundation Model capabilities to improve generalized anomaly detection, building more approachable fraud controls, creating safer payouts, and developing user-facing solutions that prevent costly pricing mistakes and make merchant checkout setup easier.

About Mesh

At Mesh, our mission is to enable consumers to pay and be paid with any asset. Today, trillions of dollars in tokenized assets exist but remain largely unusable for everyday commerce. Mesh is bridging this gap by making crypto payments reliable, useful, and ubiquitous. We combine a powerful orchestration engine with a seamless consumer app to unlock liquidity for the world. Backed by leading investors like SBI, Money Forward, Paradigm, Dragonfly, Galaxy, and PayPal Ventures, we are building the infrastructure for the next era of the global economy. Join us!

Overview

Mesh is seeking our first Head of Card Product.

Crypto solved receiving value. It has not solved spending it. Hundreds of millions of people hold crypto they cannot use to buy fuel or groceries. Every previous fix asked the merchant to change... new software, new assets, new risk... and merchants declined. The result is a vicious cycle: because crypto is not spendable, consumers do not hold much of it. Because consumers do not hold much of it, merchants do not accept it.

We are breaking the cycle from the other side. A user pays with crypto. The merchant receives an ordinary card payment. Nothing changes at the point of sale, so everything changes for the consumer: crypto becomes spendable at over a hundred million merchants in more than two hundred countries overnight... including the markets where people are already paid in stablecoins and have nowhere to spend them. It stops being an asset you hold and becomes money you use.

You will own this program end-to-end: the consumer experience, the bank partnership, the network relationship, and the compliance framework that makes it real. Card programs are not won with code. They are won by earning the confidence of banks and networks, which is why so few companies can build this. If you have spent your career learning how card programs really work, this is the seat where that knowledge changes what money can do.

What You'll Do

  • Own the card program end to end. You are the single accountable owner of this product ... its launch, its growth, its economics. If it touches the program, it's yours.
  • Earn the confidence of banks and networks. You will sit across from bank officers, network compliance teams, and regulators ... in every market the program touches ... and get to yes on KYC, fraud, refunds, and every edge case of how money moves. You write the specificity a bank signs. This is hands-on work, not delegated work.
  • Make paying with crypto feel effortless. Provisioning a card into a wallet, confirming on device, recovering from a failed or disputed transaction. You decide what the user believes is happening and make every screen and state consistent with that belief.
  • Win distribution through wallet partners. This product only matters if wallets carry it. You pitch it, shape each integration, and make partners successful ... their volume is the scoreboard.
  • Decide what cards become at Mesh. Today it is one program. New programs, networks, geographies, and commercialization are yours to figure out ... and to argue for at the exec table with evidence.

Who You Are

  • Experience: You have owned a regulated financial product that shipped through a bank partner or regulator ... a card program, a lending product, a banking or money movement product. Card program experience is a strong plus, not a requirement.
  • Compliance Fluency: You have earned a compliance sign-off from a bank partner, network, or regulator ... KYC, AML, transaction monitoring, fraud, disputes. You can describe a decision a bank pushed back on and how you got to yes.  Experience across multiple markets or regulatory regimes is a strong plus.
  • Consumer Product Judgment: You have owned a consumer payments or fintech product and its outcome ... volume, activation, retention, or P&L. You can walk through a flow you shipped and the reasoning behind it.
  • Mobile Payments: You have shipped device-level payment experiences ... secure element or secure enclave integration, push provisioning, token requestor work with the networks. 
  • AI Leverage: You use AI daily to draft program documentation, model economics, and automate the operational work of running a program.
  • Crypto: Ideally, you have built products that integrate into crypto wallets like MetaMask, Trust Wallet, or Phantom.

descriptions.job-1anwnlr:
About Mesh

At Mesh, our mission is to enable consumers to pay and be paid with any asset. Today, trillions of dollars in tokenized assets exist but remain largely unusable for everyday commerce. Mesh is bridging this gap by making crypto payments reliable, useful, and ubiquitous. We combine a powerful orchestration engine with a seamless consumer app to unlock liquidity for the world. Backed by leading investors like SBI, Money Forward, Paradigm, Dragonfly, Galaxy, and PayPal Ventures, we are building the infrastructure for the next era of the global economy. Join us!

Overview

Mesh is looking for an exceptional leader to build and scale our Forward Deployed Engineering (FDE) organization — a new function at the company, starting with you. We have a strong preference for someone who resides in the New York City area or San Francisco. 

Reporting to our CTO, you'll lead a team of senior engineers who embed directly with a small, capped set of our most strategic partners — exchanges, neobanks, and prediction markets that drive the lion's share of our volume. These partners aren't buying a static product off the shelf. They're buying working crypto rails inside their product, against their brokers, their compliance posture, and their release schedule. The gap between a demo that works and a production integration that survives contact with a partner's environment is where deals stall, and where generic support queues and quarterly roadmap cycles fail.

Our thesis is simple: FDE sits inside Engineering, not in a services org. An FDE ships code that lands in the account and when it generalizes in our core platform. Engagements are time-boxed with a clear "ship something working end-to-end" milestone — not open-ended residencies. And the function stays deliberately small. The moment it needs a manager of managers, it has stopped being FDE and become consulting with an engineering badge. Holding that line is a core part of the job.

This role requires equal parts technical judgment, commercial acumen, and organizational leadership. You need to be technical enough to earn immediate credibility with a partner's top engineers, scope an integration live on a call, and call out a bad architectural decision — but your leverage comes from the team you build and the alignment you drive, not from the code you personally write.

What You'll Do

Build and scale the FDE organization

  • Define the operating model: engagement shape, deployment cadence, scoping standards, and hiring bar
  • Hire at least 2-3 senior and staff-level generalists this year placed close to the partner engineering team and timezone they support
  • Be open to running the first engagement(s) yourself to prove the playbook, then scale it through the team

Own delivery at our most strategic accounts

  • Be the person a partner's VP of Engineering or CTO calls — run integration reviews, hold commitments, and turn stalled technical conversations into signed plans
  • Assign named owners, not a rotating pool: one engineer or small pod per account, with a mapped executive sponsor
  • Own the qualification bar. FDE is justified when integration is the bottleneck, the account can absorb a dedicated engineer, speed decides the deal, or the pattern generalizes to the next ten partners
  • Set the boundary with Customer Success, who own the relationship, and Support, who own break-fix. CS flags what an account needs; you decide whether it's an FDE build, a platform ask, or neither
  • Measure partner growth, volume, and time-to-production — not tickets closed

Shape product and platform strategy

  • Turn the sharpest signal in the company — what partners need in production — into scoped, prioritized platform input
  • Enforce the productization ratchet: what's built either generalizes into our shared platform inside a defined window, or we stop re-investing in it. Guard against both failure modes — a silent per-customer fork, and a core roadmap hijacked by one-off asks
  • Build reference architectures, QA, and monitoring that catch failure modes inside the integration rather than in a support queue

Who You Are

Leadership and team building

  • 10+ years in technical roles, with 4+ years leading forward-deployed teams
  • Experience building a 0→1 organization or a new service line inside an existing company
  • A track record of attracting, developing, and retaining senior engineers in a competitive market, including personally closing candidates

Technical credibility

  • You came up as a strong backend or integrations engineer and can still read a codebase, whiteboard a system, debug a design, and review architecture alongside your team. You are not expected to be in the codebase day to day
  • Substantial experience with broker, exchange, or payments integration patterns and crypto rails. Our partners' engineers will spot someone learning the domain on the job in the first meeting
  • A history of embedding with customer engineering teams to deliver complex technical work in production

Commercial and strategic acumen

  • Strong executive presence — effective and composed in front of partner executives and our own leadership team, including when an integration is on fire
  • Client-facing instincts: you like being in front of partners, can read a room, and can separate the stated ask from the real constraint
  • Willingness to push back. You've declined bad requests from partners and internal stakeholders alike, and driven alignment across engineering, revenue, and product without escalating every disagreement
  • Experience defining engagement models, scoping, and pricing for technical delivery work

For candidates outside of New York or San Francisco, compensation will be adjusted to reflect the applicable market and location-based pay band. The base salary range listed excludes commission (if applicable), equity, and benefits. The pay range represents the minimum and maximum target for new-hire compensation. Actual compensation may vary and may be higher or lower depending on individual circumstances.

Why You’ll Love It Here

At Mesh, you're not stepping into a typical role—you're joining a rocket ship in mid-liftoff. You'll tackle complex, meaningful problems that actually move an industry forward, working alongside a sharp, motivated team that moves quickly, collaborates deeply, and expects everyone to operate with ownership. This is the kind of place where you'll see your work ship fast, make real impact, and be able to point to something and say, "I built that." You'll grow fast, level up your skills, and get a front-row seat to how a high-growth company scales from the inside, with competitive comp, solid benefits, and room to stretch your craft all coming standard. If you're energized by building, learning, and shaping something big—this is where you'll want to be.

In-Office Expectations

Employees based in our San Francisco, New York, and Bangalore hubs are expected to work from the office at least 40% of the time (approximately two days per week). This expectation may vary slightly depending on role, team, and business needs. Certain roles that require closer cross-functional collaboration or operational support may have additional in-office requirements, which will be discussed during the interview process. Our hybrid approach is designed to balance meaningful in-person collaboration, team building, and real-time decision-making with the flexibility to work remotely. We believe this structure supports strong execution while preserving autonomy and focus time.

How We Care For Our Team

We believe great work happens when people feel valued and supported. That starts with competitive salary and equity that grows as you and the company grow, plus comprehensive health coverage for you and your family. We offer unlimited PTO—and we mean it. Take the time you need to recharge and show up at your best.

We're invested in your growth with a dedicated budget for courses, conferences, and certifications. Work from wherever you're most productive with our remote-friendly approach, and count on having the top-tier tools and equipment you need to do exceptional work.

About Polymarket

Polymarket is the world's largest prediction market platform. We enable individuals to express views on real-world events by trading on outcomes across politics, economics, sports, culture, and current affairs. Built as a peer-to-peer marketplace with no centralized "house," Polymarket aggregates diverse opinions into transparent, market-based probabilities that reflect collective expectations about the future.

We're growing fast, both in terms of volume ($21B traded in 2025) and adoption as an alternative news source. Our ambition is to become a ubiquitous beacon of truth in global media and we need your help adding fuel to the fire.


About the Role

Polymarket is launching perpetual futures and we're looking for Senior Backend Engineers to own the core systems that make it run. This is backend exchange engineering in the truest sense: low-latency order matching, high-throughput order state management, and the infrastructure that keeps an exchange operating correctly under load.

Ownership here is real and broad. We're looking for engineers who have built and operated order-book-based exchange systems before and can step in with deep context, take meaningful ownership of critical backend components, and raise the reliability and performance of the platform as we scale. If you've worked on the backend of a serious exchange and want to do it again somewhere with momentum, this is the role.


What You'll Do

  • Own core exchange backend systems. Take deep ownership of the systems that power order matching, position management, and order state across perpetual futures.

  • Build and optimize the matching engine. Profile hot paths, reduce lock contention, and drive improvements to latency and throughput backed by benchmarks and production-grade evidence.

  • Design for correctness at scale. Build queueing and backpressure mechanisms that keep the orderbook consistent and reliable under high load, without crossing books, creating ghost fills, or introducing stale order state.

  • Build for observability. Instrument systems with metrics, logs, and traces. Establish rollback guarantees and narrow critical paths that make production incidents faster to detect, diagnose, and resolve.

  • Improve runtime performance. Optimize CPU, memory, and allocation behavior to meet the demands of a high-throughput exchange in production.

  • Own production incidents end-to-end. Debug latency and correctness issues directly, and drive follow-through that leaves the system measurably better each time.


What We're Looking For

  • Senior backend engineering experience with a strong background in order-book-based exchange systems

  • Deep knowledge of low-latency systems: concurrency, lock contention, async correctness, and performance profiling

  • Experience with matching engines, order state management, or similar exchange infrastructure

  • Comfort working in Rust or a strong willingness to work in it — enthusiasm for the language is a plus, resistance to it is a red flag

  • Strong observability fundamentals: metrics, logs, distributed traces, and profiling tools

  • Strong computer science fundamentals: algorithms, data structures, and systems design

  • (Plus) Experience with high-frequency or low-latency trading infrastructure

  • (Plus) Familiarity with Redis, PostgreSQL, gRPC, and Protobuf

  • (Plus) Kubernetes and AWS production operations experience

This range reflects a good-faith estimate for this position. Experience levels vary widely within a title here, so please reach out even if your expectations fall outside it. We're always happy to chat.
